chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has land upon which there is a known land tax (kharaj), which sometimes increases and sometimes decreases, so he gives it to a man on the condition that he pays the land tax for him and gives him two hundred dirhams in the year, he said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.خَرَاجٌ: Land tax or tribute paid to the government or landlord
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to lease land where the tenant pays a fixed fee and covers the variable land tax?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific form of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping/lease) where the tenant assumes the risk of variable land tax (*kharaj*) in exchange for a fixed annual payment of two hundred dirhams. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic flexibility in agricultural contracts, distinguishing between fixed rent and variable tax burdens, and underscores the permissibility of transferring fiscal risk to the cultivator as long as the core elements of the contract are clear.
